record.notes: Released on 29 February 2024; the TC260 notice was posted on 1 March 2024. The technical document was written to inform a future national standard; it revised a draft for comment of October 2023, adding among other things a supply-chain security assessment of the hardware and software underlying generative AI models. Its content was raised to the recommended national standard GB/T 45654-2025 (CN-10), published 25 April 2025 and effective 1 November 2025, which replaces it. The secondary URL is an unofficial English translation by CSET.

verification.note: CAUTION: not confirmed on an official page. The official URL now serves the TC260 homepage (plain, browser-rendered and print copies stored on 14 October 2026), which no longer shows the notice or the document. The stored CSET translation page confirms the Chinese and English titles, TC260 as issuer, original publication on 29 February 2024, the earlier October 2023 draft and the document's purpose of informing a future national standard. The posting date of 1 March 2024 rests on the timestamp in the official URL. The identifier TC260-003 and the replacement by GB/T 45654-2025 are not shown in the stored files; status 'Superseded' is an assessment based on the publication of GB/T 45654-2025 (CN-10), and no formal TC260 withdrawal notice is known.

legal_force.quote: This document applies to service providers carrying out safety assessments and improving their safety levels, and also provides the relevant main oversight department (主管部门) a reference for judging the safety levels of generative AI services.

notes.quote: One notable addition to this documentation, relative to a preliminary draft released in October 2023, is a clause requiring a supply chain security assessment of Chinese generative AI models’ underlying hardware and software.

judgment.status_reasoning: No change. The stored official copies are the TC260 homepage and say nothing about this document. The CSET page shows that the technical document was designed to inform a future national standard and lists a draft national standard on the same subject (December 2024). The record's 'Superseded' rests on the publication of GB/T 45654-2025 (CN-10, effective 1 November 2025), which none of this run's stored files show; I keep 'Superseded' because nothing stored contradicts it and the successor is a record in the register, but the stored evidence only partly supports it.
judgment.scope_reasoning: Clearly in scope: a government standards committee's technical document setting security requirements and safety assessments for generative AI services.
